transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Welcome, welcome! Quality Quidditch Supplies, at your service. What can I do for you today, Mr. Potter? Looking for a new broom, perhaps? Or just browsing our latest Comet-brand polish?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Er, no, actually, I'm here to return something. I bought a broom-servicing kit from here the other day, and... well, it's not up to standard. The handle polish is dried out, and the tail-twig clippers are rusted. It's not really usable like this.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Oh, dear, I'm terribly sorry to hear that, Mr. Potter. That certainly doesn't sound like the quality we pride ourselves on. Let me just see... do you have your receipt there, and the kit itself? We can certainly have a look.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Sure, here's the receipt. And... yes, here's the kit. I was looking forward to using it, too. I just want to get it replaced or get a refund, whichever is easier. It's not like I want to make a big deal out of it or anything.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, yes, thank you, Mr. Potter. Let me just... ah. I see you've opened the kit. All the components are out of their original packaging. Now, this is a tricky one, I'm afraid. You see, all servicing kits are non-refundable once the seal is broken, Mr. Potter. It's a health and safety regulation, stops any cross-contamination, you understand. You'll have to take it up with the manufacturer directly — that's a six-week owl exchange minimum, usually, for something like this.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I don't understand. It's not like I used the stuff or anything. I just opened it to check it, and then I noticed it was no good. Why can't you just replace it or give me a refund? It's not fit for purpose! I've bought plenty of stuff here before, and it's always been fine. This is the first time I've had a problem, and it's not even my fault!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I do understand your frustration, Mr. Potter, truly I do. And we certainly appreciate your custom over the years. However, the policy on servicing kits is very strict, precisely because of the nature of the items inside. Once the seal is broken, we simply cannot accept them back into stock. It's a standard practice for this type of product, you see, to ensure everything we sell is completely pristine and untouched for the next customer.

It's not that we doubt your word at all, but rules are rules, especially when it comes to things like broom maintenance that affect performance and safety. Your best course of action really is to contact the manufacturer directly with your receipt. They're usually quite good about replacing faulty items, though as I said, it does take a while for the owl post to sort it all out. They'll have a different returns procedure than we do for sealed products.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I see. I wasn't aware of this policy. But... it's just not really fair, is it? I mean, I haven't even used the stuff. It's just... broken. I don't have time to wait six weeks for an owl post, and I don't even know how to get in touch with the manufacturer. This is supposed to be a simple thing, and now it's turning into a big hassle. I just... I don't want to cause trouble, but this doesn't seem right.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I understand, Mr. Potter, and I genuinely sympathise. It certainly feels unfair when you've done nothing wrong and just want a working product. The manufacturer's contact details should be on the packaging itself, usually a small parchment scroll tucked inside, or sometimes printed directly on the main box. If you give me the name of the kit, I might be able to find their address for you in our supplier catalogue.

I know the six-week wait is a pain, especially with Quidditch season approaching, but that really is the established channel for these particular items once they've been opened. It's a tricky situation, and I wish I could do more directly from here, but our hands are tied by the supplier agreements and health regulations for servicing kits.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Okay... thanks for trying to help, I guess. I'll look for the contact details on the packaging. It's just... a bit of a letdown, you know? I was really looking forward to fixing up my broom. Oh well, I suppose that's how it goes sometimes. I'll... I'll just go and sort it out with the manufacturer, then. It's not the end of the world, I suppose. Thanks for your time, anyway.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I do understand, Mr. Potter. It's always a letdown when you're looking forward to something and it doesn't quite work out. I truly am sorry for the inconvenience this has caused you. If you can tell me the exact brand of the kit, I can certainly try to confirm the manufacturer's name and address for you, just to make sure you have the correct details before you send that owl. It's the least I can do.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The brand... let me think. It was a... a... Oh, I can't remember, actually. I bought it in a bit of a rush. It was one of the cheaper ones, I think. I'm sorry, I should have paid more attention. It's all written down in my account book at home, but I don't have it with me. I'm not usually so... absent-minded, but... well, you know, with everything that's been going on...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: No need to apologise, Mr. Potter, not at all! We keep excellent records here at Quality Quidditch Supplies. If you purchased it recently and put it on your account, I can certainly look up your past purchases for you. That way we can identify the specific kit and, most importantly, the manufacturer. Give me a moment, if you will, and I'll check our ledger for you. What name would it have been under? Just "Potter"? And roughly when did you make the purchase?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, just "Potter" would be right. I... I can't remember the exact date, but it was definitely within the last week. Maybe... around four days ago? No, wait, that's not right. It was after I... after we... never mind. It was pretty recent, anyway. Thanks for checking, it's a bit embarrassing, but I'm really grateful you can help. I appreciate it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Not at all embarrassing, Mr. Potter, not in the slightest! Happens all the time, especially when there are so many excellent products to choose from. Let's see here... "Potter"... within the last week... Ah, yes, here we are!

You purchased the 'Nimbus Nurture' Servicing Kit, just four days ago, exactly as you thought. And the manufacturer for that particular kit is "Broomcare Innovations Ltd." Their main office is in Kempton, and their owl post address is generally on the product's small instruction parchment, as I mentioned. If you don't have that, I can give you their general customer service owl post address from our supplier book:

Broomcare Innovations Ltd.
Customer Services
The Whispering Willows Business Park
Kempton-upon-Styx
KM6 3BB

That should be everything you need to send them an owl. Again, I truly am sorry for the hassle, and I hope they get it sorted for you quickly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, really. You've been very helpful, considering... well, considering the situation. I'll send the owl to Broomcare Innovations as soon as I can. I hope it doesn't take too long, but I suppose I'll just have to be patient. It's better than nothing, I suppose. I'll... I'll go and get the rest of the information I need from home and send the owl. Thanks again for your help, it's much appreciated.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
You're very welcome, Mr. Potter. I'm glad I could at least help with the manufacturer's details. Do let me know if you run into any further trouble contacting them, though they're usually quite responsive, even if the exchange itself takes a little time. We always aim to help where we can.

Come back and see us again soon for any *other* Quidditch needs you might have! And I truly hope Broomcare Innovations gets that kit sorted for you promptly. Safe flying!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will do, thanks. I... I hope to be back under better circumstances next time. It's been... a bit of a rough day, all told. But hey, at least I've still got my broom, even if it's in need of some care. I'll get it sorted. Thanks again for the information, and... and for not making me feel too bad about this. Have a good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
You're most welcome, Mr. Potter. And I completely understand. Some days just have a few more bludgers than others, don't they? But that's the spirit! A good broom is worth a bit of extra effort, and I'm sure it'll be flying perfectly once you get that kit sorted.

You have a good day yourself, and do stop by again whenever you're in the area. Perhaps next time for a look at our new line of Chudley Cannons fan merchandise! Take care, Mr. Potter.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Sure, I'll do that. Fan merchandise sounds... intriguing. I've heard of Chudley Cannons, of course, but... well, you know, I've always been a bit more of a... different team fan. But it's cool to have options, I guess. I'll definitely be back for that. Thanks again for... everything. See you around!
